record_title: A sharp Euclidean solution-error barrier for symmetric GMRES(1)
scientific_context: For unpreconditioned GMRES(1)/minimal residual iteration on any real symmetric nonsingular linear system, the Euclidean solution error can increase on an indefinite problem but by at most the sharp factor 2/sqrt(3) in one cycle. A two-dimensional equality case repeats the maximal spike every other step while its residual contracts on every step.
limitations: Exact arithmetic, real symmetric nonsingular matrices, ordinary Euclidean norm and restart-one minimal residual iteration only. The bound is not asserted for consecutive full MINRES/full GMRES iterates, arbitrary preconditioning, finite precision or nonsymmetric matrices. It is a per-cycle transient bound and does not imply global convergence on indefinite systems. Older minimum-residual/minimum-error literature leaves residual historical-equivalence risk.
